--- title: "Initial phoneme isolation" subtitle: "Automatically generated task sheet · CF_IDENTIFICACION_FONEMA_INICIAL" --- ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} **Automatically generated task sheet** (A · Accuracy; quality class A). Generated on November 27, 2026 with `scripts/R/ficha_generica_v3.R --tarea CF_IDENTIFICACION_FONEMA_INICIAL`. Figures come from the data; the theoretical framework is shared by the tasks of the same construct. **Interpretation and team review are missing.** Spanish name: *Identificación del fonema inicial*. [Spanish version](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/auto/CF_IDENTIFICACION_FONEMA_INICIAL.html). ::: **In one sentence.** Initial phoneme isolation, from age 5 to 6 (1,981 administrations in 4 cohorts; 2 forms). Stability across time points ρ = .27. AUC .56–.78 against persistent reading difficulty. ## Description | | | |---|---| | Codes | 1675 1896 | | Battery | LEEDUCA | | Format | forced choice | | Items | 11 (1896); 20 (1675) according to the platform | | Task family | A · Accuracy | | Score | Correct responses | | Instructions (platform) | The child says the initial sound in the CVC o CCVC syllables pronounced by the experimenter. | ## How it is programmed on the platform The platform is the reference: what the activity actually presents is what is measured. Configuration read from the activity itself on 23/10/2026 (without modifying it). Cell contents are in Spanish. | Code|Name on the platform |Presentation | Test items| Practice items|Example items |Time limit |Order |Scoring | Age.term (label 3)| |----:|:--------------------------|:------------------------------------------------------------|----------:|--------------:|:-------------|:----------|:-----|:--------|------------------:| | 1896|Identificar fonemas |Un estímulo por pantalla; el evaluador marca acierto o error | 11| 0|— |— |fijo |Aciertos | 5.1, 6| | 1675|Identificar fonema Inicial |Un dibujo o lámina por pantalla | 20| 4|— |— |fijo |Aciertos | 5, 6| **Differences from the dictionary or the instructions (in Spanish):** - **1896.** 11 sílabas CVC/CCVC; las instrucciones hablan de 10. - **1675.** 4 ejemplos + 20 dibujos. *Age.term: provisional reading of the activity's label 3 (3rd digit = age, 4th = term; 0 = annual), to be confirmed with the engineer.* **How it looks on the platform** (first item or example; 2026 screenshot; the interface is in Spanish). ::: {layout-ncol=2} ![1675 · Identificar fonema Inicial](../../figuras/plataforma/1675.jpg){.lightbox fig-alt="Screenshot of activity 1675"} ![1896 · Identificar fonemas](../../figuras/plataforma/1896.jpg){.lightbox fig-alt="Screenshot of activity 1896"} ::: ## Theoretical framework Phonological awareness is the ability to reflect on and manipulate the sounds of speech. The platform's tasks cover a continuum of difficulty: - by **unit**: syllable or phoneme; - by **operation**: counting, identifying, segmenting or deleting; - by **position**: initial, final or any. The "all positions" version mixes items and is the most demanding. **What the evidence says:** - **Phonemes and manipulation are what most distinguish dyslexia.** In 2,252 children from six European languages, phoneme deletion and RAN were the strongest concurrent predictors of dyslexia [@landerl2013predictors]. In consistent orthographies, children with dyslexia perform below even younger readers of the same reading level on phoneme manipulation tasks, but not on syllable tasks [@parrila2020rlmatch]. - **In Spanish, phonological awareness develops in stages**, from the syllable to the phoneme. Phonemic awareness builds on learning to read and at the same time drives it: the relation is reciprocal [@denton2000pa]. Phonological awareness predicts above all the reading of complex syllables [@martinez2020silabica]. - **Its predictive value is universal, but changes with age.** Phonemic awareness, letters and RAN predict reading growth equally in Spanish, Czech and English [@caravolas2013growth]. Its relation with fluency, however, is more complex and depends on task and age, whereas RAN predicts fluency in all languages [@landerl2019pa]. This is what @catts2026definicion lead us to expect: precursors are useful for early prognosis and lose weight once there is reading to measure. The pilot task sheets develop this framework in more detail: [syllable counting](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/CF523.html) and [rapid naming](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/RAN.html) (*in Spanish*). **What our data show.** The pattern matches the literature: - **What predicts best.** Deletion tasks in all positions are those that best predict low Woodcock-Muñoz fluency (median AUC .72–.73, up to .81). - **In between.** The other deletion and identification tasks (.63–.68). - **What predicts least.** Phoneme segmentation and syllable counting (.60–.62). - **Consistency and stability.** Internal consistency is good (α = .82–.94), but stability between terms is low (ρ = .27–.41). Many tasks were given in only one or two sessions, and children change quickly at these ages. For an individual decision, the result should be confirmed at two time points. ## Sample and descriptive statistics | Time point| Form| Cohort| Session|School year | N| Non-Preleo| Preleo| Schools| |----------:|----:|------:|-------:|:-----------|---:|----------:|------:|-------:| | 5.2| 1675| 2010| 130|2015/16 | 151| 61| 89| 30| | 5.2| 2012| 2011| 156|2016/17 | 192| 0| 192| 32| | 5.2| 1675| 2013| 629|2018/19 | 89| 51| 38| 26| | 5.2| 1675| 2014| 907|2019/20 | 72| 4| 68| 16| | 6.1| 1896| 2010| 152|2016/17 | 919| 263| 655| 34| | 6.1| 1896| 2013| 898|2019/20 | 558| 398| 160| 35| | Form| Time point| N| Cohorts| Mean| SD| Median| Skewness| % floor| % ceiling| |----:|----------:|---:|----------------:|----:|----:|------:|--------:|-------:|---------:| | 1675| 5.2| 116| 2010, 2013, 2014| 6.06| 3.14| 7| -0.39| 5.17| 4.31| | 1896| 6.1| 661| 2010, 2013| 8.95| 3.14| 11| -1.64| 3.93| 50.83| **Score range** (non-Preleo group, in correct responses). The usual range goes from P1 to P99 (98% of the children). The minimum–maximum is the one observed after cleaning; the possible range is 0–11 correct responses. | Form| Time point| N|Usual range (P1–P99) |Min.–max. |Possible range | Warning| |----:|----------:|---:|:--------------------|:---------|:--------------|-------:| | 1675| 5.2| 116|0–11 |0–11 |0–11 | | | 1896| 6.1| 661|0–11 |0–11 |0–11 | | ## Reliability Stability across time points in the same children: ρ from .27 (median .27, 1 pairs of time points). Internal consistency in the 2021 analyses: α = .92. | Cohort| From| To| n| r| ρ| |------:|----:|---:|---:|----:|----:| | 2010| 5.2| 6.1| 132| 0.27| 0.27| ## Validity **Concurrent.** With other tasks in its own domain (Phonological awareness), r = .23–.70. Outside its domain, the highest relation is with: Oral morphosyntax (5.2, r = .26); Word and text reading (6.1, r = .56). **Against reading difficulty and comprehension.** Against persistent difficulty, AUC .56–.78. Against poor comprehension one or two school years later (non-circular criterion), AUC .56–.61. ![Validity: AUC with 95% confidence interval (labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_CF_IDENTIFICACION_FONEMA_INICIAL_F2_validez.png){width=85%} **Against an external criterion, years later.** Against low Woodcock-Muñoz reading fluency in 2021/22 ([chapter](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/criterio-woodcock.html), *in Spanish*), AUC .63–.63 (2 time points; 430–654 children). ## Provisional norms | Form| Time point| N| Cohorts| P5| P10| P16| P25| P50| P75| P90| |----:|----------:|---:|----------------:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1675| 5.2| 116| 2010, 2013, 2014| 0.8| 1| 2| 3.8| 7| 9| 10| | 2012| 5.2| 192| 2011| 0.6| 2| 3| 4.8| 7| 9| 11| | 1896| 6.1| 661| 2010, 2013| 1.0| 3| 6| 8.0| 11| 11| 11| Each form (platform code) has its own norms, because the forms need not measure on the same scale. These are norms by time point (school year × term). For dates between assessments and time points without a normative sample, study M3 proposes continuous norms on **months of instruction**, not on age, with relative age within the school year as an adjustment. ![Provisional norms (non-Preleo schools; labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_CF_IDENTIFICACION_FONEMA_INICIAL_F1_baremo.png){width=85%} ### Forms: can they be pooled? Forms given at the same time point are compared. They are considered **equivalent** if the mean difference is smaller than 0.20 SD and the SD ratio is between 0.80 and 1.25. If the same children took them, **linear equating** is also computed, which puts the second form on the scale of the first, together with the correlation between forms (parallel-forms reliability). If the groups differ, the difference mixes form and cohort. | Time point| Form 1| Form 2|Comparison | d (2 − 1)| SD ratio|Verdict |r between forms |Equating | |----------:|------:|------:|:----------------|---------:|--------:|:----------|:---------------|:--------| | 5.2| 1675| 2012|different groups | -0.09| 1|equivalent |— |— | ## Variables that affect it |Variable | Time point| n| Effect| p| |:---------------------------------------|----------:|-----:|------:|-----:| |School SES (ρ) | 5.2| 491| 0.018| 0.683| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 5.2| 485| 0.066| 0.467| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 5.2| 486| 0.040| 0.384| |School (ICC) | 5.2| 504| 0.038| | |School SES (ρ) | 6.1| 1,477| 0.144| 0.000| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 6.1| 1,473| -0.015| 0.769| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 6.1| 1,474| 0.012| 0.642| |School (ICC) | 6.1| 1,477| 0.160| | ## For publications The LEEDUCA platform task “Initial phoneme isolation” (codes 1675 and 1896; LEEDUCA battery) assesses phonemic awareness (initial phoneme isolation). The child selects a response among the options presented on the screen. It comprises 11 items. The time limit is 120 seconds. It is administered individually on a computer at school. In the 2010, 2011, 2013 and 2014 cohorts it was administered in 6 sessions, from 5 to 6 years of age. The main outcome is the number of correct responses. In our data (2021 analyses), internal consistency was α = .92 (N = 1,546, 11 items). Stability across successive administrations (median interval of 8 months) was ρ = .43 (median of 2 session pairs; range .40–.47). Stability across time points was ρ = .27. Against later poor reading comprehension, AUC = .56–.61. ## Pending issues - Ceiling effect at 6.1 (form 1896) (more than 15% of children with the maximum score). - The task has 2 forms; in 0 of 1 comparisons they have different scales. Norms are given by form (see "Forms"). - La puntuación máxima observada (24) supera el número de ítems (11): puede que se puntúen los ítems de ejemplo, que haya una versión con más ítems o un error de datos. Comprobar antes de describir la tarea y distinguir ítems de prueba y de ejemplo. *(Spanish)* - Write the interpretation; review with the team.
